# Introduction {#sec-introduction}

## Data sources

| Source | Access | Used for |
|--------|--------|----------|
| CPS Wikibase | SPARQL, `https://cps.tibwiki.io/query/proxy/sparql` | Works, materials, persons, exhibition, catalogue |
| Wikidata | SPARQL, `https://query.wikidata.org/sparql` | Context about the artist and linked entities |
| DNB | SRU, `https://services.dnb.de/sru/dnb` (MARC21-xml) | Publications by and about the artist |

All queries are stored as `.rq` files in `src/baldessari/queries/` or as strings in the Python package `baldessari`, so they can be reused outside the book.

## Data model of the CPS Wikibase

Each CPS item has one or more *types* (property P3). An item can carry several types at once: a work may be both an *artwork* and a *painting*. The figures below therefore count items per type and do not add up to the total number of items.

@tbl-types and @fig-types show how the knowledge graph is composed. The CPS data describe a catalogue of works together with the materials and persons needed to describe them.

## Catalogue used as a source

Much of the data was derived from the exhibition catalogue @baldessari1999. It is itself an item in the CPS Wikibase and is linked to the DNB (see [Chapter -@sec-dnb]).
